title: Designing Quality MPI Correctness Benchmarks: Insights and Metrics
problem: MPI correctness benchmarks suffer from imbalanced distributions of correct versus erroneous codes, complicating metric interpretation. Many tools detect errors but lack helpfulness features like reporting affected source lines or error classifications.
motivation: Reliable benchmarks are essential for systematically evaluating and improving MPI correctness detection tools widely used in high-performance computing.
method: The paper identifies metric interpretation challenges in imbalanced datasets and extends the true positive definition with stricter variants that assess tool helpfulness, specifically whether tools report source lines and error classes. It introduces a noise metric to quantify distracting false error reports. These metrics are empirically evaluated on MPI-BugBench using three tools: ITAC, MUST, and PARCOACH.
key_novelty: Stricter true positive variants that account for tool output quality and usefulness combined with a noise metric to measure distracting error reports.
contributions: Extended true positive definitions considering tool output quality and helpfulness
Noise metric for quantifying false and distracting error reports
Empirical evaluation framework on MPI-BugBench for ITAC, MUST, and PARCOACH
Analysis of metric interpretation challenges with imbalanced benchmark datasets
limitations: Paper focuses on MPI correctness tools; generalizability to other programming models and domains is not discussed.
primary_theme: MPI correctness benchmark quality and evaluation metrics
